exposure: indications for cesarean delivery (previous CD, atypical/abnormal fetal surveillance, malposition/malpresentation, non-progressive first stage of labour, non-progressive second stage of labour)
cohort: The study included all pregnant persons in Ontario who delivered a live- or stillborn infant weighing >=500 g at >=20 weeks gestation between April 1, 2012 and March 31, 2019.
finding: The overall cesarean delivery rate in Ontario slightly increased over 7 fiscal years (2012-2013 to 2018-2019), with Robson group 5 (term, singleton, cephalic pregnancy with previous CD) and indications like previous CD, atypical fetal surveillance, and malpresentation being the largest contributors.
mod_finding: The study found a slight increase in overall cesarean delivery rates over time, with specific Robson groups and indications such as previous CD and malposition/malpresentation identified as key drivers contributing to this mode of birth.
